$ power smart list
rc 0
--- out
  native  - PredatorSense default: Balanced on power, Eco on battery, nothing else (no load or heat logic, like Native auto)
  truesense  - Our profile for this laptop: Balanced day to day, Performance when you game, Turbo only when sustained and cool, Eco on battery
  steady  - For long games and cooling that is not the laptop's own (external fans): Performance when busy, never Turbo, and it changes mode only after minutes of quiet
  battery-first  - Longest battery and quietest: no Turbo, light modes everywhere
  performance-first  - Fastest: Performance for everyday use on power, Turbo after 10 s of heavy load
  silent  - As quiet as possible: Quiet and Balanced only, no Turbo
--- err
=== end

$ fan curve list
rc 0
--- out
  native  - PredatorSense default: the firmware controls the fans exactly as it does on Windows (they stop when cool). Nothing of ours runs
  truesense  - Our curve for this laptop: silent when cool, early and smooth ramp, full speed before throttling
  quiet  - Lowest noise: the fans stay off longer and ramp later
  performance  - Cooler and louder: starts early and ramps hard
  max-cooling  - Fans at full speed above 60 C
--- err
=== end

$ gpu undervolt list
rc 0
--- out
  native      offset   +0 MHz  cap  none  - PredatorSense default: no offset and no clock cap
  truesense   offset +120 MHz  cap  2400  - Our profile for the RTX 4060 Laptop: a moderate curve shift with a clock cap, aiming for less power and heat at about the same speed. Unverified on your unit: test under load
  mild        offset  +60 MHz  cap  2500  - Very safe: small shift, high cap
  cool        offset +100 MHz  cap  2100  - Cooler and quieter: lower cap, bigger shift
  efficient   offset +150 MHz  cap  1800  - Lowest power for light gaming: some games will run slower
--- err
=== end
